Al Jazeera — published 24 Sep 2026 12:25 EDT? (page metadata: published 2026-09-24T12:25:20, last updated 16:24) — by Faisal Ali

HEADLINE: Fighting widens across Ethiopia as Tigray clashes escalate

QUOTE (Abdisalam Balema, member of the TPLF central committee, by phone from Mekelle, Wednesday morning): "They've begun an offensive around southern Tigray. They're carrying out strikes in many places. We are not sure of the extent of it or whether they will continue, but we will assess it."
A day later Balema told Al Jazeera the situation had become a "full war".

Fighting intensified across parts of Tigray and later spread to the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions, pitting federal forces against several armed groups. Lower-level clashes had been ongoing for weeks with frequent federal drone strikes.

The Tigray Army said the federal government had launched a "full-scale offensive" involving infantry, mechanised units and drones, and said its forces had begun counteroffensive operations. Getachew Reda, a former senior TPLF figure who now advises PM Abiy Ahmed, gave the opposite account, accusing the TPLF of launching the attack.

Tigrayan forces seized airports in the region and Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights across Tigray. Local reports said they had captured Abala, a district capital in neighbouring Afar.

The escalation came days after seven armed movements, including the TPLF, announced the Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival, committed to removing Abiy's government. It brings together the Amhara Fano National Movement and the Oromo Liberation Army, alongside movements from Somali, Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz areas.

The regional East African bloc IGAD called for hostilities to cease and direct dialogue to resume; the UN has expressed concern over the new armed coalition and reports of drone attacks.
About three-quarters of a million people were already internally displaced in Tigray because of the earlier war, according to UN migration data.

QUOTE (Balema): "We've been forced to ally with other movements who also face an existential threat from the government. We don't want a repeat of 2020 when we were encircled and alone."
QUOTE (Balema): "We have a political charter, and our aim is to remove the personalist regime of Abiy Ahmed, establish a transitional government, hold a constitutional dialogue and move to elections."
QUOTE (Getachew Reda, to state media this week): "I don't lose sleep over that." And: "Now it [the TPLF] goes back to the drawing board, and declares Pretoria dead and starts an alliance with the very people who fell out with the federal government because Pretoria was signed."
QUOTE (Abiy Ahmed, to lawmakers in July): "Let alone Eritrea, the TPLF and Sudan, even if others were added, we do not have an iota of fear regarding Ethiopia's sovereignty."
QUOTE (Faisal Roble, regional analyst, East African Parliament member): Pretoria "changed the equation". "Abiy alienated all of them at different levels."

Ethiopian government spokeswoman Billene Seyoum told Reuters the alliance's members had already been collaborating with financial backing from Asmara. Eritrea repeatedly denies supporting Ethiopian armed groups.
Regional dimension: Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has visited Asmara twice since July; RSF commander Hemedti reportedly visited Addis Ababa in late August.

AFP (via France24 wire, 24 Sep): Tigray rebels told AFP they were in a state of "full-blown war" with the federal government; the 2020-2022 civil war killed more than 600,000 people according to African Union estimates.
